_about: Curated additive reference keyed by E/INS number (lower-case, no prefix). risk: none|low|moderate|high for the general population. not_permitted_in: regions (IN, EU, US) where it is not authorised in food. Conditions map a user condition to a stricter level. Review and extend this file — it is the source of truth, not the LLM.

101.name: Riboflavin
101.note: Vitamin B2 used as a yellow color.

102.name: Tartrazine
102.note: Synthetic azo dye. EU labels must warn it 'may have an adverse effect on activity and attention in children'. Can trigger reactions in some aspirin-sensitive people.

104.name: Quinoline Yellow
104.note: Synthetic dye carrying the EU hyperactivity warning. Not authorised in food in the US.

110.name: Sunset Yellow FCF
110.note: Synthetic azo dye carrying the EU hyperactivity warning.

120.name: Carmine
120.note: Red color made from insects — not vegetarian. Rare allergic reactions.

122.name: Carmoisine
122.note: Synthetic azo dye carrying the EU hyperactivity warning. Not authorised in food in the US.

124.name: Ponceau 4R
124.note: Synthetic azo dye carrying the EU hyperactivity warning. Not authorised in food in the US.

127.name: Erythrosine
127.note: The US FDA revoked its authorisation in food in January 2025 (cancer findings in male rats). The EU allows it only in cocktail and candied cherries.

129.name: Allura Red AC
129.note: Synthetic azo dye carrying the EU hyperactivity warning.

150a.name: Plain Caramel
150a.note: Caramel color made by heating sugar.

150c.name: Ammonia Caramel
150c.note: Caramel color made with ammonium compounds.

150d.name: Sulphite Ammonia Caramel
150d.note: Common in colas. Can contain 4-MEI, a by-product IARC lists as possibly carcinogenic (Group 2B).

160b.name: Annatto
160b.note: Natural color from annatto seeds; occasional allergic reactions.

171.name: Titanium Dioxide
171.note: EFSA (2021) concluded it can no longer be considered safe as a food additive because genotoxicity could not be ruled out. Banned in EU food since 2022.

210.name: Benzoic Acid
210.note: Preservative; can form benzene with vitamin C in drinks.

211.name: Sodium Benzoate
211.note: Preservative; can form small amounts of benzene with vitamin C in drinks exposed to heat or light. Was part of the Southampton hyperactivity study mixture.

220.name: Sulphur Dioxide
220.note: Sulphites can trigger asthma symptoms in sensitive people and must be declared as an allergen.

223.name: Sodium Metabisulphite
223.note: Sulphite preservative; can trigger asthma symptoms in sensitive people.

224.name: Potassium Metabisulphite
224.note: Sulphite preservative; can trigger asthma symptoms in sensitive people.

249.name: Potassium Nitrite
249.note: Curing salt for processed meat; can form nitrosamines. IARC classifies processed meat as carcinogenic to humans (Group 1).

250.name: Sodium Nitrite
250.note: Curing salt for processed meat; can form nitrosamines. IARC classifies processed meat as carcinogenic to humans (Group 1).

251.name: Sodium Nitrate
251.note: Curing agent in processed meat; converts to nitrite.

252.name: Potassium Nitrate
252.note: Curing agent in processed meat; converts to nitrite.

319.name: TBHQ
319.note: Synthetic antioxidant in fried snacks and oils; EFSA ADI 0.7 mg/kg bw. Animal studies raise questions about immune effects.

320.name: BHA
320.note: Synthetic antioxidant classified by IARC as possibly carcinogenic to humans (Group 2B).

322.name: Lecithin
322.note: Emulsifier, usually from soy or sunflower. Check the source if allergic to soy.

338.name: Phosphoric Acid
338.note: Acidifier in colas. Added phosphate is absorbed almost completely — a concern for kidney disease and bone health at high intakes.

407.name: Carrageenan
407.note: Seaweed-based thickener. Still permitted, but EFSA (2018) asked for more data; some animal studies link it to gut inflammation.

420.name: Sorbitol
420.note: Sugar alcohol; laxative in larger amounts.

433.name: Polysorbate 80
433.note: Synthetic emulsifier; mouse studies show it can disturb gut bacteria and promote low-grade inflammation.

440.name: Pectin
440.note: Fruit fibre used as a gelling agent.

466.name: Carboxymethyl Cellulose
466.note: Synthetic thickener; animal and early human studies suggest it can disturb the gut microbiome.

471.name: Mono- and Diglycerides of Fatty Acids
471.note: Common emulsifier, often palm-derived; may contain small amounts of trans fat.

476.name: PGPR
476.note: Emulsifier used to cut cocoa butter in chocolate.

508.name: Potassium Chloride
508.note: Salt substitute; adds potassium, which matters in kidney disease.

621.name: Monosodium Glutamate
621.note: Flavor enhancer considered safe by regulators; adds sodium. A few people report short-lived symptoms.

627.name: Disodium Guanylate
627.note: Flavor enhancer; a purine source, relevant for gout.

631.name: Disodium Inosinate
631.note: Flavor enhancer; a purine source, relevant for gout.

635.name: Disodium 5'-Ribonucleotides
635.note: Flavor enhancer; a purine source, relevant for gout.

904.name: Shellac
904.note: Glazing agent from insects — not vegan.

924.name: Potassium Bromate
924.note: Flour improver classified by IARC as possibly carcinogenic (Group 2B). Banned as a food additive by FSSAI (2016) and in the EU.

950.name: Acesulfame K
950.note: Non-sugar sweetener. WHO (2023) advises against non-sugar sweeteners for weight control.

951.name: Aspartame
951.note: IARC classified it as possibly carcinogenic (Group 2B) in 2023; JECFA kept the ADI at 40 mg/kg bw. Contains phenylalanine — must be avoided with PKU.

952.name: Cyclamate
952.note: Non-sugar sweetener; not authorised in food in the US.

954.name: Saccharin
954.note: Non-sugar sweetener. WHO (2023) advises against non-sugar sweeteners for weight control.

955.name: Sucralose
955.note: Non-sugar sweetener. WHO (2023) advises against non-sugar sweeteners for weight control; stability when baked is debated.

965.name: Maltitol
965.note: Sugar alcohol common in 'sugar-free' sweets. Raises blood sugar less than sugar, but not zero; laxative in larger amounts.

1422.name: Acetylated Distarch Adipate
1422.note: Modified starch used as a thickener.

1442.name: Hydroxypropyl Distarch Phosphate
1442.note: Modified starch used as a thickener.

1450.name: Starch Sodium Octenyl Succinate
1450.note: Modified starch used as an emulsifier.
